0.0.n: 採点する becomes 採点しよう to suggest checking the score together.

0.2.n: キミ is a casual, familiar way to address the viewer.

0.3.n: は marks the viewer as the topic of the question.

0.4.n: 何 asks the number, and 問 counts questions.

0.5.n: 正解 combines with できた to talk about answers the viewer managed to get right.

0.6.n: できた is the past form of できる, expressing ability or successful completion.

0.7.n: か helps form the gentle question ending かな.

0.8.n: な joins か in かな, giving the question a curious, conversational tone.

1.0.n: コメント refers to the video's comment section here.

1.1.n: で marks comments as the means of sharing your result.

1.2.n: 教えて is the て-form of 教える, used here as a casual request.

1.3.n: ね makes the request sound friendly and inviting.

2.0.n: 問 is the counter used for questions or quiz items.

2.1.n: 以上 includes the stated number, so exactly 21 also qualifies.

2.2.n: 正解 pairs with できた to describe successfully answering questions.

2.3.n: できた is past tense; the phrase before キミ describes what the viewer achieved.

2.4.n: キミ is casually addressed as someone who got at least 21 questions right.

2.5.n: は marks the viewer described by the preceding phrase as the topic.

2.7.n: ロゴ combines with マスター to form the quiz's achievement title.

2.8.n: マスター describes an expert here, not a person's name.

2.9.n: だ is the plain, casual form used to declare that someone holds this title.

3.0.n: おめでとう is a casual congratulatory expression; adding ございます makes it more polite.

4.0.n: 次回 refers to the next installment of the quiz.

4.1.n: の links 次回 to クイズ, identifying which quiz is meant.

4.2.n: クイズ is a borrowed word written in katakana.

4.3.n: も adds the next quiz as another thing to look forward to.

4.4.n: お楽しみ combines with に in a set expression encouraging anticipation; お adds politeness.

4.5.n: に completes お楽しみに, a shortened expression asking viewers to look forward to something.

4.7.n: チャンネル combines directly with 登録 to refer to subscribing to the video channel.

4.8.n: 登録 literally refers to registration; with チャンネル, it means subscribing.

4.9.n: を marks チャンネル登録 as the thing not to forget.

4.10.n: 忘れないで uses the negative form of 忘れる plus で to ask someone not to do something.

4.11.n: ね softens the reminder and makes it friendly.

5.0.n: また signals that the speaker hopes the viewer will return for another attempt.

5.1.n: キミ addresses the viewer casually and familiarly.

5.2.n: の links キミ with チャレンジ, showing whose attempt it is.

5.3.n: チャレンジ refers to the viewer taking on another quiz, not challenging the speaker.

5.4.n: を marks the viewer's attempt as what the speaker is waiting for.

5.5.n: 待ってる is casual 待っている: the て-form of 待つ plus いる, with い dropped.

5.6.n: よ adds an upbeat assurance directed at the viewer.

0.lit: Let’s score! As for you, how many questions were you able to answer correctly, I wonder?
0.tip: かな makes the question sound curious and friendly rather than demanding.

1.lit: In the comments, tell us, okay!
1.tip: A て-form verb can stand alone as a casual request.

2.lit: You who could answer 21 questions or more correctly are a logo master!
2.tip: The description before キミ identifies the viewers who qualify; there is no explicit word for if.

3.tip: Add ございます after おめでとう when you want a more polite congratulation.

4.lit: Look forward to next time’s quiz too! Don’t forget channel subscription, okay!
4.tip: A negative verb ending in ないで can make a request not to do something.

5.lit: Again, I’m waiting for your attempt, I tell you!
5.tip: 待ってる drops the い from 待っている, a very common shortening in casual speech.
